records.text: A mechanical harvest golem.

A Defias Brotherhood smuggler in Westfall who invokes the Brotherhood’s power, threatens opponents and welcomes a chance to use a freshly sharpened blade. Gryan Stoutmantle’s People’s Militia targets the smugglers in its effort to defend Westfall.
A Riverpaw taskmaster that growls about fresh meat and welcomes more bones to gnaw on.
A mechanical Harvest Watcher that has taken over farmland. Farmer Saldean asks for the watchers to be cleared from his own and neighboring fields.
A mechanical harvest reaper.
A Riverpaw gnoll that growls about fresh meat and more bones to gnaw on.
A Defias Brotherhood pathstalker who meets intruders with threats and boasts of a freshly sharpened blade. In combat, the pathstalker uses Backstab.
A Defias Brotherhood highwayman who meets intruders with threats and boasts of a freshly sharpened blade. In combat, the highwayman uses Backstab.
A Riverpaw gnoll mongrel that snarls about fresh meat and bones to gnaw. When fighting, it uses Spirit Decay.
A Riverpaw gnoll brute that snarls about fresh meat and bones to gnaw. Its combat technique is Demoralizing Shout.
A Riverpaw gnoll overseer, encountered among the pack in the Dagger Hills. It snarls about fresh meat and bones to gnaw, and initiates a spoken aggro line.
A coastal murloc named among the threats Captain Grayson wants cleared from Westfall’s shore for sailors’ safety. In combat, the Coastrunner uses a poisonous stab.
A coastal murloc named among the threats Captain Grayson wants cleared from Westfall’s shore for sailors’ safety. The Tidehunter fights with Frost Nova.
A coastal murloc named among the threats Captain Grayson wants cleared from Westfall’s shore for sailors’ safety. When badly hurt, the Warrior flees for assistance.

Farmer Saldean refuses to abandon his Westfall land despite the thieves who drove other farm folk away. He speaks proudly of the Saldeans staying in Westfall and asks for help clearing Harvest Watchers from his fields and neighboring fields. He also points experienced fighters toward Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia, which protects Westfall's farmlands.

Gryan Stoutmantle leads the People’s Militia, which defends Westfall’s farms and people from the Defias. He returned to his homeland after serving on the battlefields of Lordaeron and resents Stormwind’s abandonment of Westfall. He recruits fighters to help reclaim the countryside and regards the militia’s cause as a defense of local freedom.

Salma Saldean cooks at the Saldean farm in Westfall. She prepares Goretusk liver pie and Westfall stew, and asks for ingredients to make them. When Verna Furlbrow sends her stew recipe, Salma welcomes the chance to make it; she describes Verna warmly and expects to miss her when she leaves Westfall for Stormwind.

Theodore Furlbrow is a Westfall farmer whose land was taken by ruffians, forcing him and his wife, Verna, to leave. He is trying to repair their wagon so they can get out of Westfall, and hopes to reclaim the farm deed if they return. His missing pocket watch matters because Verna’s father gave it to him on their wedding day. He points capable travelers toward Gryan Stoutmantle and the People’s Militia, which he says protects Westfall’s farmlands.

Verna Furlbrow is a Westfall farmer displaced from her land with her husband, Theodore. As they wait for their wagon to be repaired so they can leave, she worries about their tired horse, Old Blanchy, and asks for oats. She also shares her Westfall stew recipe with Salma Saldean, reflecting a wish to help a neighbor even as the family prepares to leave the homeland she never expected to abandon.

Grimbooze Thunderbrew is a brewer in Westfall who makes requests in playful rhymes. Grimbooze seeks hops for a rich lager, grain for an amber brew and truesilver to fashion a still. The verses describe an amber-colored lifelong love and a private stash, and end with a toast to Grimbooze and the helper.

Old Murk-Eye leads murloc raids along Westfall’s shore. Captain Grayson blames him for driving the lighthouse keeper’s family away, then leading a second attack that killed them after their return. Grayson seeks his death to end the threat to the lighthouse.

Captain Grayson died on Westfall’s rocks and now works to spare sailors the same fate. He witnessed Old Murk-Eye’s raid kill the lighthouse keeper’s family; with no one left to tend the flame, Grayson takes responsibility for it. He asks for oil to keep the beacon lit and for help clearing murlocs from the coast, including Old Murk-Eye, so sailors reaching the beaches will be safer.

A Defias knuckleduster, this Brotherhood fighter meets attackers with threats of retaliation, boasts about the Brotherhood, or remarks on a freshly sharpened blade. In combat, the knuckleduster can use Pummel.
A Riverpaw bandit who greets a fight with hungry threats about bones and fresh meat, then attacks with Backstab. Its combat speech and tactics mark it as a brutal close-range pack raider.

A Riverpaw mystic sharing the bandits’ hungry threats about bones and fresh meat, but striking with Lightning Bolt. The title and ranged spell distinguish this spellcaster from the pack’s close-range raiders.
A young murloc oracle who casts Lightning Bolt in combat and can answer nearby allies’ need with Healing Wave. When badly hurt, it may flee for help.
A murloc hunter that summons a crawler while out of combat, then fights with its own attacks. The script shows a hunting companion, without establishing any further personal history.
Vultros is a beast that uses Swoop in combat.

The Defias Traitor offers to guide Gryan Stoutmantle's allies to VanCleef's hideout in exchange for protection. He knows the hidden entrance in Moonbrook and fears the Defias gang will kill him for cooperating. Suspicious of a lone escort's strength, he urges bringing friends and keeping close, and calls for help when threatened.
Rusty Harvest Golems are mechanical harvest golems that attack with Tetanus in combat.
Defias Footpads invoke the Brotherhood when threatening opponents and relish the chance to use a freshly sharpened blade.
Protector Bialon serves in the People's Militia.
Protector Weaver serves in the People's Militia.
Protector Dutfield serves with the People’s Militia in Westfall.
Protector Gariel serves with the People’s Militia in Westfall, reporting Defias activity on the coastal horizon and giving the all-clear for Sentinel Hill.

Quartermaster Lewis struggles to keep Sentinel Hill supplied amid frequent action. With little direct aid from Stormwind and dwindling armor stocks, Lewis relies on Osric Strang’s shop, Limited Immunity, in Old Town. Lewis thanks those who deliver armor, promises to distribute it promptly to those in need and encourages them to return to help Sentinel Hill.
A Riverpaw scout of Westfall who growls about fresh meat and more bones to gnaw on.
A Riverpaw herbalist of Westfall who growls about fresh meat and more bones to gnaw on.
Benny Blaanco is a humanoid who tries to flee for help when badly hurt.

A Defias trapper of Westfall, among the bands Gryan Stoutmantle reports disrupting the farms and Jangolode Mine area. The trapper threatens opponents in the Brotherhood’s name, boasts of its power and welcomes a chance to use a freshly sharpened blade.
Sergeant Brashclaw is found in Westfall and growls about fresh meat and more bones to gnaw on.
A murloc netter in Westfall.
A murloc raider in Westfall.
A murloc oracle on the Westfall coast. Captain Grayson regards these murlocs as a threat to sailors reaching the beaches.
Slark is a rare humanoid who tries to flee for help when badly hurt.
Brack is a rare humanoid who tries to flee for help when badly hurt and can cast Hamstring, Strike, and Pierce Armor in combat.

Thor is Sentinel Hill’s gryphon master. He offers rides to Stormwind for a fee and confidently recommends the route for delivering Lewis’s note to Osric Strang. He treats an urgent delivery as no trouble and calls his fare worthwhile.

A Defias messenger in Westfall who threatens death to anyone standing in the way. The messenger taunts opponents with a “special message” demanding their death and boasts of delivering them to the afterlife.
Leprithus is an undead creature in Westfall.
Foe Reaper 4000 is a mechanical creature in Westfall.

Old Blanchy is a working animal cared for by Verna Furlbrow. In Verna’s Westfall account, Blanchy is tired after their hard work; Verna fed her before leaving the farm, but the unexpected wagon breakdown leaves them seeking more oats for her.

A Defias Brotherhood pillager in Westfall. Gryan Stoutmantle reports pillagers plundering the Gold Coast Quarry, Moonbrook and Alexston Farmstead. Their own threats praise the Brotherhood’s power and warn that it will not tolerate opposition.

A Defias Brotherhood looter in Westfall, targeted by Gryan Stoutmantle’s People’s Militia. The looter boasts of the Brotherhood’s power, warns against opposition and eagerly welcomes a chance to use a freshly sharpened blade.
A Defias Brotherhood henchman in Westfall who threatens opposition with the Brotherhood’s power and eagerly welcomes a chance to use a freshly sharpened blade.
A brainwashed noble in Westfall.
Marisa du'Paige is a rare humanoid whose combat repertoire includes Fireball, Polymorph: Chicken, Sleep, and Chains of Ice.
A Defias conjurer in Westfall.

A chicken with an unusual befriending and feeding interaction. It looks up quizzically, clucks and scratches at the ground in a way an observer thinks might spell “SALDEAN.” It waits hungrily for special chicken feed and is described pecking at it.
An undead skeletal miner in Westfall.
An undead excavator in Westfall.
An undead dynamiter in Westfall.

Foreman Thistlenettle is an undead foreman in Westfall and Wilder Thistlenettle’s brother. Wilder recalls that his brother was among those missing after a mine beneath a Moonbrook barn collapsed, and that he always carried an Explorers’ League badge.

Scout Riell serves the People’s Militia at Sentinel Hill and wants to reclaim the land from the Defias. She identifies bandana material as a sign of rank and directs adventurers against the high-ranking members she expects in VanCleef’s hideout. She asks for red silk bandanas as proof and salutes those who help the militia.

Captain Danuvin of the People’s Militia defends Westfall as his homeland. He says Stormwind has abandoned it but refuses to abandon its remaining citizens, describing the defenders as former farmers making a stand. He asks adventurers to patrol against gnolls he suspects work with Deadmines thieves and reports Defias movement in Moonbrook to Lord Stoutmantle.
A Defias digger in Westfall who invokes the Brotherhood’s power and warns opponents that it will not tolerate their actions.
The Dust Devil is an elemental that uses gusts of wind while fighting. Collin Mauren seeks dust devil debris from Westfall for a messaging-spell experiment.
A coyote packleader is an animal identified by its role leading a pack; it can use a furious howl in combat.
A lumberjack in Westfall.
Gina MacGregor sells trade supplies at Sentinel Hill in Westfall.
A rotten ghoul in Westfall.
Protector Dorana is a protector of the People's Militia in Westfall.
Protector Deni is a protector of the People's Militia in Westfall.
Protector Korelor serves with the People’s Militia.
Protector Leick is a protector of the People's Militia in Westfall.

Scout Galiaan is a People's Militia scout at Sentinel Hill who has tracked the Defias Front over time. Galiaan studies the gang's movements and uses the red leather bandanas worn by many of its members as identifying clues, asking for a collection to support that intelligence work.
A Riverpaw shaman encountered in combat, this gnoll calls its foes fresh meat and bones to gnaw on, then uses Lightning Bolt against them.
Fleshrippers are hostile beasts found across several regions. In combat, they can use Muscle Tear against their foes.
Shore Crawlers are hostile beasts found in coastal areas. In combat, they use a specialized attack against their foes.
A kobold digger fiercely guards its candle, cries out in fear when threatened, and pleads not to be killed. When badly hurt, it may flee for help; it can also use Pierce Armor in combat.
Master Digger is a rare humanoid who can use Heroic Strike in combat.
A Riverpaw miner who greets attackers with hungry threats about bones and fresh meat. Its brief combat cries give this hostile worker a blunt, predatory voice.
William MacGregor is a bowyer in the human settlement at Northshire. He sells goods, including ammunition, and can repair equipment; his name and trade mark him as a local craft merchant.
A Defias merchant styled the Free Wheeling Merchant, this profiteer offers goods and repairs.
Mike Miller is a bread merchant in Westfall.
A Defias watchman who can shoot at opponents at range.

A Defias magician encountered among the Defias in Westfall, it uses frost armor before combat, hurls fireballs in battle, and can summon a living flame. Its arcane training marks it as a magical combatant in the gang’s ranks.
A Defias worker found among the gang’s forces in Westfall, this worker is a combatant despite the name, and flees for assistance when badly hurt.
Kriggon Talsone is a fisherman in Westfall who sells goods to visitors. His work combines fishing with running a small local shop.

Daphne Stilwell lives on the Westfall coast while her husband Jordan is away in Ironforge. When Defias threaten her home, she welcomes help but remains ready to defend it herself, armed with her own gun. She directs the stand near the house and fights alongside her protector. Afterward, she asks that Duthorian Rall be told she is safe so he can reassure Jordan. Her gratitude reflects relief for her family and property, and she praises the helper’s courage.
A Westfall woodworker found in the region’s countryside.

Agent Kearnen conducts a concealed stakeout of a Defias tower in Westfall and briefs agents sent by Mathias. She has observed a shipment from Duskwood guarded by nonhuman creatures, but does not know what those guards are. She asks an infiltrator to obtain the key, investigate the chest and report the findings to Mathias.
This malformed humanoid belongs to the Defias and is designated a drone.

Defias tower patrollers complain of aching feet and unsettling creatures below. In an exchange with Raven, a patroller asks for a break but reluctantly returns to patrol. They use Torch Burn in combat.

Klaven Mortwake revels in the prospect of Stormwind's fallen defenders rising to fight for the Brotherhood, boasting that two will rise when one dies. Klaven consults tomes and searches for Venture Company formulations, while threatening a rogue with the claim that fear can be smelled.
Defias tower sentries serve as guards.
An undead Venture Co. Drone found in The Barrens and Westfall.
Known as the Protector of the People, this figure is associated with the People's Militia.
Innkeeper Heather welcomes weary travelers to her inn and offers help, lodging and goods.
Christopher Hewen is a trade-supplies vendor. He offers goods to visitors in the area.
Stable Master Kirk Maxwell offers help with stabling pets and recovering lost companions. His greeting addresses visitors directly and presents both kinds of assistance.
Elder Skychaser reflects on an older hunting tradition pursued for glory and honor, and wonders whether the present is so different. The elder also offers a way to ask about other elders.

The Westfall Flame Warden tends an Alliance festival fire and urges visitors to honor Alliance flames across the lands. The Warden speaks openly against the Horde’s fires, encouraging their desecration as part of the midsummer rivalry.
